questions.prompt: The program crashes while flushing a batch. What does the file look like?
options: Every line is lost, because the file was open
Every line before the last one is complete JSON, and the last line may be cut off
questions.explanation: Each flush only adds lines at the end. A crash can cut the line being written, but the lines above it were already complete.

questions.prompt: Why does runStep flush before a tool runs, not only before a model call?
options: Because the tool reads the session file
Because a tool can change files, so the record of its call must be on disk first
Because the model needs the tool result on disk
Because flushing makes the tool run faster
questions.explanation: If the program dies while the tool changes the world, the file must still show that the call started. Flushing first puts the tool/call event on disk.

questions.prompt: Why is JSONL a better fit for this record than one JSON array in a file?
options: A new event is one added line, so nothing older must be written again
JSONL files are read by the model directly
JSONL removes the need for sequence numbers
questions.explanation: With one array, every change rewrites the whole file. With JSONL, adding an event appends one line, which matches an append-only log.
